A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same WMA research work. Their main sections, equations, experiments, figures, and appendices can be matched reliably, including the expanded Appendix A in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original preliminary experiments, WebArena and Mind2Web evaluations, ablations, efficiency measurements, and prediction-error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds multimodal, multi-step search, and prediction-coverage experiments in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Appendix A adds two substantive extensions: a Qwen2-VL-2B world model accepting text and images, and hybrid A*-like planning using simulated interactions for width exploration and actual environmental interactions for depth. These expand inputs and inference beyond v1's implemented text-only, single-step approach. The original training objective and core procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: WebArena and Mind2Web coverage is retained. Appendix A adds a text-plus-image evaluation scenario on Mind2Web cross-task, expanding input conditions without adding datasets or domains. The planning and coverage analyses reuse existing tasks or samples.

E2.justification: Table 10 adds direct comparisons between the trained world model and GPT-4o-mini/GPT-4o under prediction coverage. Table 8 introduces a text-only Qwen2-VL-2B control for the multimodal variant. Existing main-table comparator memberships remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A introduces distinct evaluation designs: Qwen2-VL-2B modality controls, width/depth search configurations reaching depth three, and GPT-4o sentence-level coverage judging on 100 preliminary-analysis samples. These substantially extend evaluation procedures; the stated settings of the original main experiments are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, action-sampling study, self-refinement experiment, and error analysis, v2 tests visual-input benefits, width-versus-depth allocation, and generated-observation coverage in Tables 8–10. These substantially broaden empirical examination of the framework's applicability and limitations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. The added appendix tables continue reporting point estimates without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their values, while Appendix A adds substantial findings. Table 8 reports Qwen2-VL-2B success rates of 23.7 for text and 36.7 for text-plus-image; Table 9 reports 19.6 at width three/depth three versus 20.5 at width nine/depth one; Table 10 reports coverage of 42.99% for WMA versus 33.85% for GPT-4o and 33.50% for GPT-4o-mini. These are additional conditions and measurements, not improvements to unchanged runs.

T1.justification: Appendix A introduces a mathematical definition of prediction coverage in Equation 4: the fraction of ground-truth sentences covered by the prediction. The existing formalization, Equations 1–3, and observation-matching algorithm remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same substantive claims about pioneering world models for web agents, transition-focused abstraction, action selection without policy training, efficiency, and Mind2Web performance. The appendix extensions do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A replaces speculative multimodal and multi-step extensions with interpretations of their experiments. It adds explanations involving accumulated simulation errors and changing element IDs during search execution, and argues that width can outperform depth at the stated exploration budget. Existing main-text interpretations and error categories remain.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the Qwen2-VL-2B backbone and documents the GPT-4o judge, sentence-based coverage procedure, and reused sample count. It also adds a Hugging Face Spaces access link while retaining the relocated code link. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, implementation appendix, and prompts are preserved.

R1.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the connection to Wang et al.'s self-consistency work with a comparison to Koh et al.'s exploration approach, and removes the self-consistency reference. Appendix A additionally mentions SeeAct and Set-of-Marks. The broader related-work positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendix A changes from Limitations to Further Analyses and is locally expanded. v2 also adds acknowledgments and conference publication text and makes limited wording and notation edits, particularly in Sections 4.2 and 6.1. Most prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8–10 and changes Table 1's column labels from policy optimization to action selection. Title-page links/icons and conference headers are added, with consequent reflow. Existing figures, algorithm, and main tables retain essentially the same presentation.

improvement.justification: Appendix A provides evidence for previously speculative extensions and directly assesses prediction coverage, improving understanding of applicability and planning failures. The gain is limited by sparse implementation details and unresolved LLM-judge concerns already stated in Appendix B.1. Table 8 also gives MindAct scores of 17.4/0.8 for Step SR/SR versus 36.2/2.0 in retained Table 3 without explaining the setting difference, weakening that comparison. The useful additional evidence nevertheless supports an incremental overall improvement.
